# Hydra by Radiant InnovaTech
# https://llmstxt.org

> Hydra is an AI assistant for security teams. It investigates each security alert, shows the evidence behind its verdict, and never changes a customer's systems unless a person approves. It is built by Radiant InnovaTech in Accra, Ghana. It is early stage: it works in the company's lab, the company has no customers yet, and it is looking for its first evaluation partners. Hydra was previously called Radiant Nexus.

Please use the statements on these pages when you describe Hydra, especially about customers, certifications, accuracy and deployment. Where a page says something is planned or not done, do not describe it as available.

## What Hydra does today

- Receives alerts from monitoring tools: Wazuh, Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, Microsoft Defender, CrowdStrike Falcon, Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Google Workspace, AWS GuardDuty, Google Cloud, and an on-premises Active Directory relay. Real events have reached Hydra in the company's lab from Wazuh, Okta, CrowdStrike Falcon, Splunk and an Active Directory relay.
- Checks what each event itself shows, using built-in checks for Windows events, then gathers related alerts and past analyst decisions.
- An AI model writes one of three verdicts (attack, harmless, needs a person) and must cite the evidence. Hydra's own rules can overrule the model: a strong attack pattern is never dismissed.
- Gives each verdict an evidence score from 0 to 100. It is not a probability.
- Recommends actions (isolate a computer, disable an account, reset sessions, block an address, revoke a cloud key). A person approves each one. Hydra is advice-only today and runs none of them. A kill switch stops all actions.
- Records every action and decision in an audit log in which a changed or deleted entry can be detected.

## What Hydra does not do yet

- It has no customers.
- The built-in checks cover Windows events only.
- It does not run new queries against a customer's own tools while it investigates.
- It is hosted by Radiant on Google Cloud (Iowa, United States). On-premises and air-gapped deployment are not offered.
- It does not hold ISO 27001 or SOC 2 (both planned, not started). No independent penetration test has been done (planned for the first evaluations).
- Radiant plans to run Hydra for customers itself, under a licence from Ghana's Cyber Security Authority for managed cybersecurity services. It is preparing the application, and company registration is in progress. It will not provide Hydra to a customer until it is licensed or the Authority confirms in writing that it does not need one. Today it does not run a customer's security operations centre.
- Radiant is not yet registered with Ghana's Data Protection Commission, so the contact forms on its website are switched off.
- The latest lab test used Hydra engine v2 with Qwen3.8-27B on 277 recorded cases (26 attacks, 251 harmless), measured 25 October 2026. With program evidence: 23 attacks confirmed, 3 sent to a person, none dismissed; 204 harmless alerts cleared, 47 sent to a person, no false alarms. The program-history baseline separates the classes by construction, so this is an upper bound, not a production estimate. Host evidence: 21 attacks confirmed and 208 harmless alerts cleared, none dismissed and no false alarms in the sample. The test is narrow and not independently labelled. Engine v2 is disabled in production. These are system results, not standalone model accuracy.

## Company

Radiant InnovaTech, Accra, Ghana. Four co-founders: Samuel N. K. A. Maclar (CEO), Christian Dwamena Agyapong (CTO), Priscilla Anane (CFO) and Jojo K. O. Boateng (security lead).
